cards.front: Recall a key point about Demand
cards.back: Demand is the quantity consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price over a period of time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Demand
cards.back: Law of demand: as price rises, quantity demanded falls (inverse relationship), shown by a downward-sloping demand curve.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Demand
cards.back: Factors shifting demand: income, tastes/fashion, price of substitutes and complements, population, advertising.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Demand
cards.back: Movement ALONG the curve = price change (affects quantity demanded). SHIFT of the curve = non-price factor change (changes demand at every price).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Demand
cards.back: Market demand = sum of all individual demand curves at each price level.

cards.front: What should you know about economics exam tips?
cards.back: When analysing demand changes, use the SIF framework: Shift or movement? Identify the factor. Follow through to equilibrium. Confusing shifts and movements is the most common exam error.
Change in price of the good itself (e.g. Favourable change in non-price factor)
Quantity demanded (e.g. Demand at every price)
Higher price = less real purchasing power (e.g. Higher income = more purchasing power)
Gas price rises, consumption falls (e.g. Rising wages increase restaurant demand)
Slide along existing curve (e.g. Whole curve moves right)

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A rise in income always increases demand for all goods. Correct: A rise in income increases demand for NORMAL goods but DECREASES demand for INFERIOR goods (cheaper alternatives people buy less of as they get richer — e.g. own-brand products, bus travel). Always consider whether the good is normal or inferior.
Evaluate how a recession (falling incomes) would affect demand for supermarket own-brand products and luxury restaurant meals.
AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of Demand with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: Understanding the Demand Curve and the Law of Demand
cards.back: Demand is the quantity of a good or service that consumers are willing and able to buy at a given price over a period of time. The law of demand states that, ceteris paribus (all other things being equal), as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls, and vice versa.
